Air Fryer Pork Chops

By Maike Corbett • Published: 09/25/2026
This post may contain affiliate links. Please read my disclosure policy.

Air Fryer Pork Chops are juicy boneless chops with a golden, seasoned crust, ready in about 15 minutes. No breading, no splatter, and no guessing when they are done.

Thick boneless pork chops with a smoky paprika, garlic, and onion rub.

I grew up in Germany, where pork chops and applesauce belong on the same plate. Nobody in my family ever questioned it. These come out of the air fryer, a spoonful of applesauce goes on the side, and dinner tastes like home.

Recipe Highlights

  • Ready in 25 minutes start to finish
  • Five pantry spices and no breading station
  • One flip and one basket to wash
  • High protein dinner that feeds four
  • Leftovers reheat crisp in the air fryer

Ingredient Notes

Please check the recipe card below for a detailed, printable ingredient list.

PORK CHOPS – Buy boneless chops about 1 inch thick, usually labeled center-cut loin chops. That thickness is what this recipe is built around, and it gives you a golden outside and a juicy middle. Thinner chops finish faster, so check them early.

OLIVE OIL – A light coat helps the rub stick and gives the chops their color. Avocado oil or any neutral high-heat oil works the same way.

KOSHER SALT – The full teaspoon is for Diamond Crystal. With Morton kosher or table salt, use a heaping ½ teaspoon. Like a saltier crust? Go up to 1½ teaspoons of Diamond Crystal.

SMOKED PAPRIKA – Regular paprika works if that is what you have in the cabinet. For a little heat, swap in a pinch of chili powder.

GARLIC AND ONION POWDER – Powders are the right call here. They spread evenly, cling to the oiled chops, and stay put through 15 minutes of hot air.

How To Make Air Fryer Pork Chops

Please check the printable recipe card below for more detailed instructions.

  1. Pat the pork chops dry with paper towels.
  2. Rub the chops with olive oil, then coat both sides with the seasoning.
  3. Arrange the chops in a single layer in the basket.
  4. Air fry, flip once, then rest the chops before serving.

Leftovers and Storage

STORE – Keep leftover chops in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 4 days. Store them whole when you can. Whole chops hold more moisture than sliced ones when you reheat them.

FREEZE – Cooked chops freeze well for up to 3 months in a freezer bag with the air pressed out. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator.

REHEAT – Air fryer: 350º Fahrenheit for 3 to 5 minutes, until hot all the way through. Skillet: covered, over medium-low heat, with a tablespoon or two of broth, about 5 minutes. Microwave: 30-second bursts until warm, about 90 seconds total. The air fryer brings the crust back, and the microwave works in a pinch.

MAKE AHEAD – Mix the seasoning up to a month ahead and keep it in a jar. You can also season the chops the night before, cover, and refrigerate. Pat them dry again before they go in the basket.

Serving Suggestions

WEEKNIGHT DINNER – Green Beans with Bacon cook on the stove while the chops are in the air fryer, and Sour Cream Mashed Potatoes round out the plate.

SUNDAY SUPPER – Serve the chops the way I grew up eating them, with a spoonful of applesauce and a scoop of Warm German Potato Salad.

LOW-EFFORT NIGHT – Slide Air Fryer Zucchini into the basket the minute the chops come out. The chops rest while the zucchini cooks, and dinner lands on the table together.

COOKOUT PLATE – Roasted Potatoes and a bowl of Coleslaw turn four chops into a summer dinner without lighting the grill.

Recipe Success Tips

PAT DRY – Dry chops brown. Blot both sides with paper towels right before the oil goes on, and the edges turn golden instead of gray.

THERMOMETER – An instant-read thermometer is the whole trick. Pull each chop when the thickest part reads 145º Fahrenheit, the number the National Pork Board recommends. Chops of different weights finish at different times, so start checking at 11 minutes.

SINGLE LAYER – Give the chops a little space so hot air reaches every side. A 6-quart basket holds four 1-inch chops. In a smaller basket, cook two at a time and keep the first batch warm under foil.

REST – Five minutes under a loose foil tent lets the juices settle back into the meat. Slice right away and those juices end up on the cutting board instead.

Expert Tip – Thick chops keep cooking after they leave the basket. They climb a few degrees during the rest, so 145º Fahrenheit at the pull is the sweet spot. There is no reason to push them past it.

Commonly Asked Questions

How Long Do You Cook Pork Chops in the Air Fryer?

Air Fryer Pork Chops that are 1 inch thick take 11 to 15 minutes at 400º Fahrenheit. Air fry for 6 minutes, flip, then keep going until the thickest part reads 145º Fahrenheit. Heavier chops need the longer end of that range. Pull each one as it hits temperature and give the rest another minute or two.

Do I Need to Preheat the Air Fryer?

Yes, a 5-minute preheat at 400º Fahrenheit gives the chops a better crust. The rub starts browning the moment the chops hit the hot basket. If your air fryer has no preheat button, run it empty for 3 to 5 minutes first.

Is It Safe If the Pork Is a Little Pink?

Yes, a hint of pink in the center is normal for pork cooked to 145º Fahrenheit. The USDA lowered the safe temperature for whole cuts of pork to 145º with a 3-minute rest in 2011. Trust the thermometer, not the color. Chops cooked until they are white all the way through have usually gone past juicy.

Can I Cook Frozen Pork Chops in the Air Fryer?

Yes, though thawed chops brown better and take the seasoning more evenly. Thaw them overnight in the refrigerator when you can. From frozen, expect about 50 percent more cooking time and go by the thermometer, not the clock. The rub sticks once the surface thaws, so season after the first few minutes.

What If My Pork Chops Are Thinner or Bone-In?

Thinner chops cook faster, and bone-in chops take a few minutes longer. Start checking ¾-inch chops at 8 minutes and thin ½-inch chops at 6. Bone-in chops of the same thickness usually need 2 to 3 more minutes. Either way, the thermometer makes the call at 145º Fahrenheit.

Air Fryer Pork Chops

Author: Maike Corbett
Prep Time: 10 minutes minutes
Cook Time: 15 minutes minutes
Total Time: 25 minutes minutes
Servings 4
These Air Fryer Pork Chops come out juicy in the middle with golden, seasoned edges in about 15 minutes. A quick rub of olive oil, smoked paprika, garlic, and onion powder is all it takes. No breading, one flip, and a thermometer to tell you when they are done.

Ingredients

  • 4 boneless pork chops 1 inch thick (6 to 8 ounces each)
  • 2 tablespoons olive oil
  • 1 teaspoon kosher salt
  • 1 teaspoon black pepper freshly cracked
  • 1 teaspoon garlic powder
  • 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
  • ½ teaspoon onion powder

Instructions

Prep the chops

  • Preheat the air fryer to 400º Fahrenheit for 5 minutes.
  • Pat the pork chops completely dry on both sides with paper towels.
  • Stir together the salt, pepper, garlic powder, smoked paprika, and onion powder in a small bowl.
  • Rub both sides of each chop with olive oil. Sprinkle the seasoning over both sides and press it gently into the meat.

Air fry

  • Arrange the chops in a single layer with a little space between them. Work in batches if needed.
  • Cook for 6 minutes. Flip and cook 5 to 9 minutes more, until an instant-read thermometer in the thickest part reads 145º Fahrenheit.
  • Remove each chop as it reaches temperature. Give the others another 1 to 2 minutes before checking again.

Rest and serve

  • Transfer the chops to a plate, tent loosely with foil, and rest 5 minutes before serving.

Equipment

Air Fryer
Meat Thermometer
small bowl

Notes

FOOD SAFETY

USDA guidance for pork chops is 145º Fahrenheit measured before the chops leave the heat, followed by a 3-minute rest. The 5-minute rest here covers it.
Chops of different weights finish at different times. Pull each one at 145º Fahrenheit and keep the rest going.

REST TIME

The 5-minute rest is not included in the total time.

SALT

The full teaspoon is for Diamond Crystal kosher salt. With Morton kosher or table salt, use a heaping ½ teaspoon.
